preamble: In Lovono (also called Vano), a now-extinct language of Vanikoro in the Temotu Province of the Solomon Islands, a word-final schwa reconstructed for Proto-Vanikoro corresponds to the sequence -ie. Teanu, the surviving language of the island, reduces the same vowel to -o, and Tanema has -a, so the Lovono diphthong is a local innovation rather than an inherited feature.

examples.note: Cognates are Teanu uo and Tanema uva 'greater yam (Dioscorea alata)'
With the fossilized article n-; parallels upie in showing final -ie where Tanema has -a (niava 'fire')

sources: François, A. (2021). Teanu dictionary. In Dictionaria. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. https://dictionaria.clld.org/contributions/teanu
